newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway's Saga sharply cuts costs of seismic study.
newsitem.headline: Norway's Saga sharply cuts costs of seismic study.

text.p: Saga Petroleum ASA said on Monday it had reduced the cost of acquiring seismic data to roughly 24,000 crowns sper square kilometre from about 200,000 crowns in 1990.
The company's weekly newsletter said the lower costs had been achieved on the Gjallar Ridge off mid-Norway, where Saga secured an operatorship in Norway's 15th licensing round in January.
The three-dimensional seismic data extends across four blocks covering 1,582 square kilometres.

Saga attributed the drop in seismic costs partly to improvements in technology, particularly for streamer towing, and partly to collaboration between oil companies to survey much larger areas to yield better economy of scale.
